rationale: Iteration 6 is still the best design (619.4). Its oval finishes 20/20 and its s-bend finishes 18/20. Iteration 9 (ki 0.6) lowered the s-bend finish rate to 15/20 (score 587), so ki 1.0 stays. Slalom has been stuck at progress 0.16-0.17 with 0/20 finishes across iterations 5-9, whatever was changed: speed, kp, kd, ki, and sensor size. That rules out steering gain, speed and sensor size as the main limit on slalom. Each slalom run ends with about one line-loss event, and the robot then leaves the track. The main untested lever is the line-loss recovery behaviour, which decides which way the robot turns when it loses the tape on a weave. I therefore revert to the iteration 6 design exactly and change only line_loss from last_direction to search_right. Expected result: oval and s-bend stay near iteration 6 levels, and slalom progress rises above 0.25 if recovery direction is the limit. Hypotheses: (a) slalom line_loss_events stay near 1 but progress rises; (b) if slalom stays flat, the failure is geometric, a sharp weave the 7-sensor span cannot track, and the next step is a wider span or a lower base_speed on slalom only. Measurements needed: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation, with slalom progress as the key signal.
